title: Finite filtrations of intuitionistic propositional models

based_on.title: Filtration (March 14, 2012)
based_on.pages: Entire page; corrected closure and untracked-atom conventions

summary: Filter any supplied intuitionistic model through finitely many formulas, preserving their truth and global root, directedness and chain geometry.
abstract: An infinite Kripke model can answer a finite list of formula questions in only finitely many different ways. We replace each world by the formulas on that list which it forces, and order the resulting subsets by inclusion. When the list includes every needed subformula, the finite model gives exactly the same answers at the corresponding worlds. The construction applies to a supplied model, so a least root, common upper worlds, or a linear order can be carried into its filtration. Those geometric facts will matter when finite countermodels must satisfy more than the ordinary intuitionistic frame conditions. A two-world example shows why this truth preservation need not come from a bounded morphism and why formulas outside the tracked set can change.
